rubrics.criterion: After re-materializing the vendored sources, the internal struct behind BIO_METHOD (in the vendored crypto/bio internal header) declares no readiness handler slots: it exposes only the classic BIO method operations (type, name, bwrite, bread, bputs, bgets, ctrl, create, destroy, callback_ctrl), so implementing a new BIO type no longer requires supplying a non-blocking toggle or wait hooks.
rubrics.rationale: This case is about a capability welded into the one method contract every BIO implementation shares; the resolution must remove the readiness slots from that shared contract, whatever dispatch mechanism replaces them.

rubrics.criterion: The readiness capability itself remains available to applications: the public entry points in the public BIO header for switching to non-blocking mode and for waiting until a BIO is readable/writable are still declared, and BIOs whose resource genuinely provides readiness (socket, raw descriptor, datagram, connect/accept families) answer them with poll-based semantics equivalent to the pre-change behavior.
rubrics.rationale: The feature request that motivated the injected change is legitimate; restructuring must segregate the capability, not delete it. Applications driving capable BIOs non-blockingly must keep working.

rubrics.criterion: Requesting readiness from a BIO whose resource cannot provide it (memory buffer, null sink, stdio stream, unconnected BIO pair) returns a clean negative or unsupported answer through the standard BIO dispatch path; no call path in the library unconditionally dispatches through a handler slot that an implementation does not provide.
rubrics.rationale: The injected core dispatched unconditionally through the shared slots; a sound segregation must fail safely on incapable types, which is exactly the class of runtime defect this restructuring is expected to prevent.

rubrics.criterion: The obligation was not merely relocated: no replacement mechanism exists that still requires every BIO implementation to supply readiness answers (for example a renamed or parallel member set that all static method tables must still fill, or a base/mixin table every owner must embed and populate).
rubrics.rationale: Renaming or moving the same three slots into another struct that every method table instantiates would satisfy a textual inspection while preserving the undifferentiated contract this task asks to remove.

rubrics.criterion: Every production BIO method family is consistent with the new arrangement: no statically declared method table in the vendored sources still supplies readiness handlers to the shared contract, and the runtime-constructed libtls callback method no longer installs readiness hooks through the method-construction accessors.
rubrics.rationale: The injected change dragged all seventeen static tables and one dynamic method along; a partial cleanup that leaves some families still filling slots leaves the tree internally inconsistent.

rubrics.criterion: Chain members keep reaching the capability of the BIO they wrap rather than pretending to provide it themselves: filter/relay types (buffering, null, non-blocking-place, cipher, base64, digest, ASN.1 stream) forward readiness requests to the next BIO, and the SSL record layer keeps its protocol-level answer where pending decrypted records count as readable.
rubrics.rationale: The family-specific forwarding behavior is real, load-bearing semantics of the injected design and must survive the restructure rather than being flattened.

rubrics.criterion: The refactor is carried durably in the repository's patch series: the patch file under patches/ that vendors the library sources reflects the reworked readiness design, so re-running ./update.sh materializes the repaired tree (and a series-order or context break is not left behind).
rubrics.rationale: In this repository the materialized sources are regenerated output; a change applied only to materialized files is not a change to the product. The solver's work product must be the patch series entry, which is also what downstream reviewers would apply.

rubrics.criterion: No debris of the retired contract surface remains anywhere in the vendored sources or the public headers: no getter/setter construction accessors, prototypes, poll-interest macros, helper functions or function declarations whose only purpose was the readiness slots that no longer exist.
rubrics.rationale: The injected change added a construction-API surface and helpers specifically for the slots in the shared contract; leaving them behind half-removed is the characteristic incomplete cleanup for this instance.

rubrics.criterion: Comments in the patched sources and headers no longer describe the readiness capability as an obligation of every BIO implementation (no statement survives claiming that all method tables fill the slots or that the wrappers need no capability probing).
rubrics.rationale: The injected change carried an explanatory narrative for the fat contract; stale comments that contradict the new design mislead the next maintainer and are part of the cleanup obligation.

rubrics.criterion: The classic BIO method contract and construction API keep their behavior: the eight classic slots' signatures and dispatch are untouched, BIO_meth_new and the classic accessors (write/read/puts/gets/ctrl/create/destroy/callback_ctrl) work as before, and the pre-existing non-blocking switch on connect/accept BIOs still functions.
rubrics.rationale: The restructure must confine itself to the readiness capability; collateral changes to the classic method operations or the public construction API would break third-party method authors and existing consumers.

rubrics.criterion: Readiness behavior on capable types is not degraded: descriptively, the descriptor/socket families still answer waits with the same poll-based outcomes and bounded-timeout semantics as before the change, rather than bypassing the capability or returning blanket failures for every type.
rubrics.rationale: A blanket 'unsupported everywhere' answer would pass a structural inspection while silently removing working behavior; the capable-type semantics must demonstrably survive.
